englishDefinition: To a moderate degree; fairly good or satisfactory, but not excellent.
examples: She was fairly certain that she had locked the door.
The movie was fairly entertaining, but it could have been better.
He did fairly well on the exam, considering he hadn’t studied much.
root: Derived from the adjective 'fair', which originates from the Old English 'fæger', meaning beautiful or pleasing. The adverb form began to appear in the early 14th century.

englishDefinition: the state of being vacant or unoccupied; an available position or job.
examples: The hotel had a vacancy for the weekend, so we decided to book a room.
She applied for the vacancy posted on the company's website.
There is a vacancy in the student council that needs to be filled.
root: from Middle French 'vacance', from Latin 'vacare' meaning 'to be empty' or 'to be free', combined with the suffix '-cy' indicating a state or condition.

englishDefinition: A bar or series of bars placed horizontally for use in construction, alongside or at the top of a fence, or as support for something.
examples: The train traveled smoothly along the steel rail.
He leaned against the railing while waiting for the bus.
The construction team installed the railings around the balcony.
root: Middle English reyl, from Old French rail, from Latin regula meaning "straight stick, ruler".

examples: The documentary about marine life was absolutely fascinating.
She has a fascinating story about her travels around the world.
The exhibition featured fascinating artifacts from ancient civilizations.
root: The word 'fascinating' comes from the Latin 'fascinatus', the past participle of 'fascinare', which means 'to enchant, bewitch'.

englishDefinition: A boat or ship that carries people, vehicles, or goods across a body of water.
examples: We took the ferry across the river to reach the island.
The ferry runs every hour from the mainland to the city.
She prefers to travel by ferry rather than by plane.
root: Middle English 'feri', from Old French 'ferre', from Latin 'ferre' meaning 'to carry'.

englishDefinition: As a side note; by the way; in addition to the main point.
examples: Incidentally, I heard that she got a promotion at work.
He mentioned, incidentally, that he will be traveling next week.
Incidentally, the party starts at 7 PM.
root: Derived from the Latin 'incidentalis', meaning 'occurring or likely to occur casually or by chance'.

englishDefinition: Something that is added to something else in order to complete or enhance it.
examples: She takes a vitamin supplement every day to improve her health.
The book includes a supplement with additional information.
They offered a financial supplement to help with living expenses.
root: Derived from the Latin 'supplementum', which means 'something added', from 'supplere' meaning 'to fill up'.

englishDefinition: To be vigilant or cautious; to stay alert for danger or something that may happen.
examples: Look out! There's a car coming.
You need to look out for the icy patches on the sidewalk.
If you look out for each other, you'll stay safe.
root: The phrase 'look out' combines the verb 'look' (of Old English origin) and the preposition 'out,' suggesting an outward gaze or observation.

englishDefinition: To gaze or gaze outward towards something; to observe or focus attention on something outside.
examples: She likes to look out at the ocean from her balcony.
He often looks out at the city skyline from his office.
When you look out at the mountains, you can see the beauty of nature.
root: The origin of the phrase stems from the combination of the verb "look" (Old English "locian") and the preposition "out" (Old English "ūtan"), indicating direction or focus towards the outside.

englishDefinition: Before a deadline or the expected time; early enough to avoid problems or achieve a desired outcome.
examples: She arrived in time for the meeting.
Make sure to submit your project in time to avoid penalties.
He finished the race in time to celebrate with his friends.
root: The phrase 'in time' originates from the Old English 'tima', meaning a period or season. The component 'in' suggests a sense of being within a specified period or limit.
